evidence.item: Fed implementation notes: roll over Treasury principal and reinvest MBS payments into T-bills starting Dec 1
evidence.verification_basis: Transcript references FOMC implementation notes but does not provide an exact quotation, making internal verification impossible.
evidence.source_speech_filename: 20251201_Markets are About to Do the Unexpected.txt
evidence.source_excerpt: looking at the implementation notes from the last FOMC statement, we see that beginning on December 1st, Federal Reserve will roll over at auction all principal payments from the Fed's holdings of Treasury securities, which means any treasuries that get paid back to the Fed, Fed will take that cash and just go out to the market and buy more treasuries. They won't let them bleed off their balance sheet anymore. But it doesn't stop there because again starting on December 1st, they will also be reinvesting all principal payments from the Fed holdings of agency mortgage back securities into Treasury bills.

analogies.explanation: Describes how newly printed money first benefits those closest to the money printer, causing inflation to outpace wage growth initially, but later wages catch up.
analogies.source_speech_filename: 20251201_Markets are About to Do the Unexpected.txt
analogies.source_excerpt: This is how the canon effect works. When new money gets printed, first it gets paid and goes to the hands of whoever is closest to the money printer. So, it goes to the government first, then it goes to the politically connected. As that money gets spent the first couple of times from one person's bank account to the next, prices have not yet had the time to adjust. they haven't had the increased demand from the increased amount of money in order to get bit up. But as that money gets spent through the economy, filters its way down into the paychecks and the wages of individuals, prices have now gotten bit up.
